back: A transaction left out completely: no debit and no credit. Trial balance still agrees.
Correct amount and side, but the wrong account of the same class (e.g. the wrong customer).
An amount posted to the wrong class of account, e.g. a non-current asset debited to an expense.
The wrong amount entered in the book of prime entry, so both debit and credit use the wrong figure.
Correct accounts and amount, but the debit and credit sides are swapped.
Two or more errors of the same amount that cancel each other out in the trial balance.
Old Cats Pounce On Cold Rats: Omission, Commission, Principle, Original entry, Compensating, Reversal.

front: Why are the six errors not revealed?
back: Each one changes the debit and credit totals by the same amount, or not at all, so the totals still agree.

front: Which errors ARE revealed by a trial balance?
back: Single-sided entries, unequal amounts, two entries on one side, uncancelled casting errors, balances omitted or misplaced in the trial balance.
